newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers more bullish on US debt -- MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers more bullish on US debt -- MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers subtly extended the durations of their U.S. debt portfolios over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
In the week ended April 28, the survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 106.5 percent from 106.4 percent the week before.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 43 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 42 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" held steady at 6.0 percent, unchanged from the week ended April 21.
Fifty-one percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, down from 52 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets slipped to 3.24 percent, against 3.27 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 35 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 33 percent the previous week, while 7.0 percent underweighted it. The remaining 58 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 49 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 19 percent underweighted them.
Separately, about three-fourths of the respondents in the survey said a U.S. budget agreement would not prompt them to buy more Treasuries.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
